clue.text: Motorway opponents get together for prayer

definitions.note: the insect is named for the folded forelegs that make it look like one who prays

parts.note: M is the standard abbreviation for a motorway in the UK, as in the M1
people who are against something are antis

explanation.surface: People opposed to a new motorway meet up for a prayer vigil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get together' just signals that the two pieces join. The definition is a joke: the praying insect is literally a 'prayer'.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword wit: the praying insect is named for its posture, so it can be called one who prays.

clue.text: I hesitate to interrupt wonderful new insight

indicators.note: something that interrupts breaks into the middle, so these words go inside the other piece

parts.note: ace is slang for wonderful or excellent
um is the sound someone makes when hesitating

explanation.surface: A speaker hesitates before praising some wonderful new insight.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean keen perception or shrewd understanding of a situation; they are near synonyms.

clue.text: Loud noise coming from boozy lunch — depart

indicators.note: a boozy lunch leaves the diners unsteady, so the letters of the following words stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a drunken lunch with a loud bang, perhaps a slammed door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boozy' reads as describing the lunch but signals rearranging LUNCH and DEPART together.
explanation.definitionFit: A clap of thunder is the sudden loud crash heard during a storm, an example of a loud noise.

clue.text: Vessel at beach being handy, cast off

indicators.note: off here means gone bad or out of order, so the letters of handy and cast are mixed up

explanation.surface: A boat on the beach comes in handy once it has been cast off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast off' looks like a sailing phrase, but 'cast' is fodder and 'off' alone signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A land yacht with wheels and a sail, raced across flat sands; a craft used on the shore.

clue.text: Hiss at one African — not Central, another one

parts.note: Alger Hiss was the US official accused of spying for the Soviets in the late 1940s
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: dropping the central letters of a word leaves only its outer pair

explanation.surface: Someone hisses at an African, then corrects themselves: not a Central African, another kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hiss' is not a sound but Alger Hiss, giving his first name. 'not Central' strips the middle FRIC from 'African', leaving AN; the definition is another African, not a Central one.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Algeria, a North African country, so a different kind of African from a Central one.

clue.text: Say a freight vehicle's extremely large

parts.note: an artic is an articulated lorry, a large freight truck; the 's is the link 'is'

indicators.note: extremely means take the extremes, the first and last letters of large

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a lorry is extremely large.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say a' is the definition: 'a' is an example of the grammatical part of speech, with 'Say' as 'for example'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word 'a' is the indefinite member of this grammatical class, so it is an example of one.

clue.text: Good, well-rounded projection in the theatre

parts.note: a lobe is a rounded projecting part, like an earlobe

explanation.surface: A good, rounded performance is projected in a theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: The Globe is Shakespeare's theatre on London's South Bank, hence 'the theatre'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's playhouse in Southwark, rebuilt in the 1990s, is the famous theatre with this name.

clue.text: Now and then arrest soak

indicators.note: now and then means occasionally, so take every other letter of arrest

explanation.surface: A drunkard, a soak, is arrested every so often.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soak' looks like a noun for a drunk, but is a verb: to steep flax in water.
explanation.definitionFit: A dialect and textile term: flax or hemp is steeped in water to soften the fibres.

clue.text: Into missile, stick a massive barrier

indicators.note: Into means the following pieces go inside the missile

parts.note: ASM is short for an air-to-surface missile
a wand is a thin stick

explanation.surface: A stick is pushed into a missile, oddly ending up a huge barrier.
explanation.walkthrough: The Aswan Dam holds back the Nile in Egypt.
explanation.definitionFit: The great dam on the Nile in southern Egypt is a massive structure that holds back water.

clue.text: Protestant extremely important around university? No way

indicators.note: around means the first piece is wrapped round the second

parts.note: huge can mean extremely important or great
not is a flat refusal, like no way

explanation.surface: A very important Protestant is offered a university post and refuses.
explanation.definitionFit: The Huguenots were French Calvinists, members of a Protestant movement persecuted in France.

clue.text: Capital needed by old physicist turned to advantage at first

indicators.note: turned means the physicist's name is read backwards

parts.note: James Watt, the Scottish engineer whose name is the unit of power

indicators.note: at first means take only the opening letter of advantage

explanation.surface: A capital city is wanted by an old physicist who turned it to his advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: Canada's seat of government in Ontario, so a national capital city.

clue.text: Best time to get colour back into grass

indicators.note: into means the colour goes inside the grass

parts.note: hay is dried grass

indicators.note: back means the colour word is read backwards

parts.note: dye is a colouring substance

explanation.surface: The best time of year is when colour comes back to the lawn.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's prime: the period of greatest success or vigour.

clue.text: Removing some restrictions on credit, but folding

parts.note: CR is the accountants' abbreviation for credit
easing a regime means relaxing some of its rules

explanation.surface: A government loosens lending curbs on credit, but the firm collapses anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'folding' suggests going bust, but means making creases.
explanation.definitionFit: Making creases in cloth or paper is the same as folding it.

clue.text: Rustling paperwork in the shop?

definitions.meaning: rustling is stealing cattle, also known as livestock, read here as taking stock
counting and recording all the goods a shop holds, an inventory job

explanation.surface: Papers rustle as staff do their paperwork in the shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rustling' suggests the sound of paper; it is cattle theft, since stock also means livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop's periodic inventory count, and literally the taking of livestock, which is what rustlers do.

clue.text: Logical to circulate before inhaling charlie off the radio for fun

indicators.note: to circulate here means to go round, so the logical word goes around the rest

parts.note: rational means logical

indicators.note: inhaling means taking in, so the letter for charlie goes inside

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
Charlie is the radio code word for the letter C

explanation.surface: A logical person goes round before inhaling cocaine taken just for fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charlie' is slang for cocaine, but 'off the radio' points to the radio alphabet's letter. 'to circulate' means go round, not spread.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective for activities done for leisure or enjoyment, as in recreational drugs or sport.

clue.text: Darling certainly has to walk round

indicators.note: round means the walking word goes around the other piece

parts.note: to tread is to walk
sure is an informal certainly

explanation.surface: A sweetheart is certainly expected to go for a walk around.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective, a darling possession is a cherished, much-loved one.

clue.text: Gets up again, bruised, tripping over animal's tail

indicators.note: someone tripping over falls in a heap, so these letters are jumbled
the tail of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone bruised after tripping over a dog's tail gets back up.
explanation.definitionFit: To reconstruct something is to put it up again, as with a house after a fire.

clue.text: Sobering fact: literacy is poor, dammit

indicators.note: poor means badly done, so the letters of literacy are scrambled

parts.note: heck is a mild oath like dammit

explanation.surface: Someone discovers literacy levels are poor, and swears.
explanation.definitionFit: A reminder of how things truly are, which brings someone down to earth.

clue.text: One's often foiled, giving signal to hold collapsing pack

indicators.note: to hold means the signal word wraps round the rest

parts.note: a cue is a signal to act, as for an actor

indicators.note: collapsing means the letters of pack fall into disorder

explanation.surface: A plot is foiled when a signal reveals the gang is collapsing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foiled' suggests a thwarted plan; it means wrapped in a foil case.
explanation.definitionFit: A small iced sponge baked in a paper or foil case, so often foiled.

clue.text: Composer changes not one note

indicators.note: not means leaving out the following item

parts.note: varies means changes
I is the Roman numeral for one
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A composer alters everything except one note.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgard Varèse was a French-born modernist who wrote music such as Ionisation.

clue.text: Started rising, being arrogant

definitions.meaning: leapt to one's feet, sprang upright in surprise
conceited and acting above one's station

explanation.surface: Someone shot to their feet, showing off their importance.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally sprang to one's feet; idiomatically describes an upstart with an inflated sense of importance.

clue.text: Revered ancestor holds social event

indicators.note: holds means the answer is contained in the words revered ancestor

explanation.surface: A revered forebear hosts a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball or party where people gather to move to music is a social event.

clue.text: Pretend to be an Indian priest

parts.note: a sham is a pretence

explanation.surface: Someone pretends to be a holy man from India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indian' suggests India, but means a Native American.
explanation.definitionFit: A medicine man among some Native American peoples, a spiritual healer and priest.

clue.text: Proclaim there's no energy to continue burning

parts.note: a fire that continues burning blazes on

explanation.definitionFit: To trumpet or publish widely, as in emblazon; a heraldic-flavoured verb for announcing.

clue.text: Spot woman's abandoned musical instrument

indicators.note: abandoned means the woman is left out of the instrument

parts.note: a zither is a stringed instrument played flat
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: A woman spots a musical instrument someone has left behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a pimple, a spot on the skin.

clue.text: As I'm about to enter, almost close loyalty scheme

indicators.note: to enter means this goes inside the other piece
almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: close weather is stuffy and without fresh air

indicators.note: about means the letters of I'm are read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone about to come in, finding it nearly stuffy, mentions a rewards scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A rewards programme giving points towards flights, a customer loyalty scheme.

clue.text: In sort of school class, take place in fear at the front

indicators.note: at the front means this piece comes first, ahead of the class
in means one word goes inside the other

parts.note: awe is reverential fear
to sit is to take one's place
RE is religious education, a school subject

explanation.surface: In a school lesson, a pupil sits terrified at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A phrase used to soften a word, meaning so to speak or in a way.

clue.text: A bank, one that is continuously troublesome

definitions.meaning: the sandbank in the North Sea named in shipping forecasts
someone who follows and plagues persistently, as trouble pursues one

explanation.surface: A bank is accused of being a constant nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: Dogger Bank is a North Sea sandbank, also a sea area in the BBC Shipping Forecast.
